quandoUsar: Advanced settings beside a title, such as build options, with a summary in `hint` that changes with the state.
“Show more” below a short list, with the `plain` variant and the trigger placed after the content.
Forms with an optional block: the content stays mounted when closed, so the fields keep their value.
quandoEvitar: Use `accordion` for a set of related sections where only one is open at a time.
Use `expandable-text` for a long paragraph clipped to a few lines.
Use `popover` when the detail should float over the page instead of pushing the content below.

teclado.acao: On the trigger, opens or closes the region.

acessibilidade: The trigger is a `<button>` with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`; the content is a `region` named by the trigger.
After closing, the region gets `visibility: hidden` and leaves the Tab order and the accessibility tree, although it stays mounted.
With `disabled` on the `Collapsible`, the trigger is disabled and the current state is kept; icon and arrow are hidden from the screen reader.
movimento: The height follows the content on a no-overshoot spring, and the content rises 8 px out of a 4 px blur as it appears.
The arrow rotates 180° on a short spring; a new click mid-animation reverses the motion from where it is.
With “reduce motion” on, the region opens and closes instantly and the color and border transitions are turned off.
desempenho: The content stays mounted even when closed, so it is rendered from the start; on a page with many `Collapsible`s with heavy content, all of that content exists at the same time.
notasIA: Assemble the three parts: `Collapsible` on the outside, `CollapsibleTrigger` and `CollapsibleContent` inside; outside a `Collapsible`, the parts throw an error.
To control it, pass `open` with `onOpenChange`; an `onClick` on the trigger that calls `preventDefault()` cancels the toggle.
`variant="card"` (default) draws a bordered surface; `plain` leaves trigger and content without a frame. Import from `@/components/ryan-ui/collapsible/collapsible`.
